lawRules.rule: I01-I12 are distinct nominal types. No identity is a type alias of another, and none converts into another implicitly.

Each identity is minted from the inputs its row lists in derivedFrom and nothing else. Changing one input changes exactly the identities that derive from it, directly or transitively, and no other: a new ReleaseId yields new FrameworkProfileId, AttachmentId, profile-qualified CapabilityId and CatalogSnapshot identities, while CarrierProfileId, SourceUnitId and RegionId stay equal. Carrier, release, attachment, project profile, configured project, snapshot and capability never vary through an input their row does not list.
lawRules.note: Case VC11 is the smallest discriminator: carrier and source fixed, ReleaseId changed. VID0T proves the change on the identities it defines (ReleaseId, FrameworkProfileId, AttachmentId) and the carrier/source/region equality; the profile-qualified CapabilityId change belongs to COX0 (I10) and the CatalogSnapshot identity change to CPF1 (I09).

lawRules.rule: The display family (a FrameworkTag value, an adapter spelling, a file extension) is presentation only. It is never a semantic dispatch key and never a cache key.

One semantic-profile or project-profile manifest declares exactly one ReleaseId. A carrier manifest declares none (I03 never contains a ReleaseId; R02 keeps CarrierProfileId equal when ReleaseId changes). A manifest naming two releases, or a versions array, is a structural manifest failure.
Separate majors are separate manifests and separate FrameworkProfileIds. Two majors of one family never share a profile, a cache key or a vocabulary table.
There is no implicit default major. A release that cannot be resolved to an exact admitted ReleaseId yields a typed unsupported-version outcome and is never coerced to the nearest or newest release.
'latest', 'next', canary and other floating tags, ranges and untagged strings never decode into a ReleaseId or any profile identity.
Activation reads the resolved installed version, never the declared range. A profile activates only on its exact release.
Each workspace package resolves its own release. Two packages in one workspace may hold different releases of one family; each gets its own FrameworkProfileId and its own cache entries.

Ambiguity is decided per claimed region, keyed by the profile-independent (SourceUnitId, RegionId). When two active profiles each mint a claim (distinct AttachmentIds) on the same RegionId and no per-file narrowing (a pragma or carrier rule) selects one, the outcome is typed ambiguous. AttachmentId stays the profile-qualified identity of one claim and is never the grouping key. No first-registered, first-loaded or newest profile wins.

A family whose admitted line is one major admits only that major. The Qwik profile admits Qwik 2 only; a resolved Qwik 1 package is unsupported-version, so Qwik-2-only behavior needs no in-profile version gate.
lawRules.note: QWK0 is docs-only and fixes the pinned release; its executable rejection proof moved to QWK1 (QWK1-ACV for the lock validator, QWK1-AC4 for activation). FWA1 keeps activation (FWA1-AC1).

lawRules.rule: Cache and audit keys over source text use (SourceUnitId, SourceRevision, ContentId) and, for maps, (SourceUnitId, SourceRevision, MapRevision). They round-trip through the canonical tagged, length-delimited encoding exactly.

Collision safety comes from the encoding, not from the digest: two tuples whose concatenated payloads coincide still encode to different bytes, and a suspected digest collision compares full canonical bytes.
Backend and process identity (CertifiedTypeEngineBinding, EngineIdentity, ProviderEpoch, session handles) stays binding-owned. It never enters a source, carrier, profile or catalog key.
Semantic caches are keyed by the exact FrameworkProfileId they compute under; syntax artifacts are keyed by CarrierProfileId and never by a semantic profile. A family-wide key is forbidden.
Profile identities are not threaded into HostConfig, CompileProfile or CodegenOptions. Consumers read them from the catalog and the demand plan.

emptyPopulations.unit: Framework release identity in kernel identities, keys and wire types
emptyPopulations.evidence: No identity, cache key or proto field carries a framework release. Two LSP loaders read a framework package version: svelte_assets gates on major 5 by string prefix (route V-D05) and vue_assets folds the exact version into an asset key (consumer V-C11). The Svelte runes/legacy choice is a per-file mode inside one release.
emptyPopulations.consequence: Nothing to delete for versions arrays or family-wide release keys; V-D01 records the implicit major and V-D05 the one ad-hoc admission.

emptyPopulations.consequence: R14 is a preservation rule; VID0T-AC4 proves the keys exclude them.
